# What this notebook does

Table 4 of the manuscript reports adjusted ML three-step odds ratios mutually
adjusting for **8 covariates** (7 binary + job satisfaction), estimated separately
in the general and hospital samples from the **shared, measurement-invariant**
four-class multiple-group model, and compared as ratios of odds ratios (ROR).

This notebook reproduces **exactly the same table with the same code path**, with a
single change: **job satisfaction is removed from the adjustment set**. Everything
else (data harmonisation, the invariant multiple-group fit, the reference class,
`ml3step_multi()`, the ridge fallback, the ROR / Cochran Q / I2 math, Holm and BH
corrections, and the output formatting) is inherited **verbatim** from
`leadership_LCA_analysis_part2_sample_comparison.qmd` rather than re-typed here, so
any drift between the two notebooks is impossible by construction.

**Motivation.** Job satisfaction is moderately to strongly correlated with
effort-reward imbalance, frequent negative acts, and self-labeled bullying. Holding
it constant conditions on a variable that is plausibly downstream of both
supervisory behavior and mistreatment, so the mistreatment ORs in Table 4 are
estimated within strata of a likely consequence of the exposure. This notebook
quantifies how much of the attenuation in Table 4 is attributable to that single
covariate.

**How the inheritance works.** The chunks of Part 2 are parsed out of the source
`.qmd` by chunk label and evaluated in order in this session. No code is copied.

---

# 0. Configuration

```{r}
#| label: config
#| results: "hold"

## IMPORTANT: Part 2's `setup` chunk begins with `rm(list = ls())`. Anything this
## notebook leaves in the global environment before that chunk runs is destroyed.
## The configuration is therefore stored in an OPTION, which survives rm(), and the
## inheritance driver runs inside local() so its own variables are out of reach.
options(nojobsat.cfg = list(
  ## Source notebook whose chunks are inherited verbatim.
  PART2_QMD = "leadership_LCA_analysis_part2_sample_comparison.qmd",
  ## The invariant multiple-group fit with n.init = 4000 is the expensive step
  ## (minutes). Cache it so re-renders of this sensitivity notebook are cheap.
  ## DELETE the cache if Part 2's data preparation or n_init ever change.
  USE_CACHE = TRUE,
  CACHE_RDS = "cache_g4_inv_part2.rds",
  ## Covariate dropped from the adjustment set.
  DROP_COV  = "job_sat"
))

local({
  cfg <- getOption("nojobsat.cfg")
  stopifnot(file.exists(cfg$PART2_QMD))
  cat("Source notebook:", normalizePath(cfg$PART2_QMD), "\n")
  cat("Dropping covariate:", cfg$DROP_COV, "\n")
})
```

# 1. Inherit Part 2's chunks verbatim

```{r}
#| label: inherit
#| results: "hold"

## ---- parse fenced R chunks of a .qmd into a named list of code strings -----
## Matches ```{r} ... ``` blocks and reads the chunk label from the '#| label:'
## option line. Chunks without a label are ignored (Part 2 labels all of them).
parse_qmd_chunks <- function(path) {
  ln    <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
  open  <- grep("^```\\{r\\b",  ln)
  close <- grep("^```\\s*$",    ln)
  out   <- list()
  for (o in open) {
    e <- close[close > o][1]
    if (is.na(e)) next
    body  <- ln[(o + 1):(e - 1)]
    lab   <- sub("^#\\|\\s*label:\\s*", "", grep("^#\\|\\s*label:", body, value = TRUE)[1])
    if (is.na(lab)) next
    ## strip the YAML-ish chunk options; keep the R code
    code  <- body[!grepl("^#\\|", body)]
    out[[trimws(lab)]] <- paste(code, collapse = "\n")
  }
  out
}

## ---- neutralise Part 2's interactive cleanup ------------------------------
## `setup` starts with `rm(list = ls()); gc()`. Evaluated here that would wipe the
## driver state mid-loop (this is what caused "objeto 'lab' no encontrado").
## Replace ONLY the rm() call, keeping the statement syntactically valid.
sanitize_chunk <- function(code)
  gsub("rm\\(\\s*list\\s*=\\s*ls\\(\\)\\s*\\)", "invisible(NULL)", code)

## Chunks required to reach the adjusted-model stage. Ordered as in Part 2.
##   setup           packages, n_init gate, seeds
##   load-data       paths, item crosswalk, cov_keys, harmonisation, `combo`
##   item-meta       behaviour type + English labels for the 13 items
##   helpers-part2   entropy, posterior list, group prevalences, item probs
##   fit-invariant   the measurement-INVARIANT four-class multiple-group model
##   per-group-post  post_g / modal_g / post_h / modal_h + alignment guards
##   shared-labels   lab_inv, ref_class (reference profile chosen from rho)
##   s3-helpers      ml3step, class_matrix, ml3step_ref, ml3step_multi
## The driver runs inside local(): `chunks`, `NEEDED` and the loop variable live in
## a temporary environment, so even a chunk that clears the global environment
## cannot destroy them mid-loop. Part 2's code is still evaluated in globalenv(),
## exactly as a normal render would.
local({
  cfg    <- getOption("nojobsat.cfg")
  chunks <- parse_qmd_chunks(cfg$PART2_QMD)
  cat("Chunks found in Part 2:", length(chunks), "\n")

  NEEDED <- c("setup", "load-data", "item-meta", "helpers-part2",
              "fit-invariant", "per-group-post", "shared-labels", "s3-helpers")

  missing <- setdiff(NEEDED, names(chunks))
  if (length(missing))
    stop("Part 2 chunk labels not found: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "),
         ". The source notebook changed; update NEEDED.")

  run_chunk <- function(lab) {
    message("== running Part 2 chunk: ", lab)
    eval(parse(text = sanitize_chunk(chunks[[lab]])), envir = globalenv())
    invisible(TRUE)
  }

  for (lab in NEEDED) {
    if (lab == "fit-invariant" && cfg$USE_CACHE && file.exists(cfg$CACHE_RDS)) {
      message("== fit-invariant: loading cached g4_inv from ", cfg$CACHE_RDS)
      assign("g4_inv", readRDS(cfg$CACHE_RDS), envir = globalenv())
      next
    }
    run_chunk(lab)
    if (lab == "fit-invariant" && cfg$USE_CACHE)
      saveRDS(get("g4_inv", envir = globalenv()), cfg$CACHE_RDS)
  }
})

stopifnot(exists("combo"), exists("cov_keys"), exists("g4_inv"),
          exists("post_g"), exists("modal_g"), exists("post_h"), exists("modal_h"),
          exists("ref_class"), exists("lab_inv"), exists("ml3step_multi"))
cat("\nInherited state OK. Reference class = raw glca index C", ref_class, " (", lab_inv[ref_class],
    "); the manuscript number is assigned in section 2b.\n", sep = "")
cat("Covariates available (Part 2 set):", paste(cov_keys, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

# 2. Drop job satisfaction from the adjustment set

```{r}
#| label: drop-cov
#| results: "hold"

## Re-materialise the config in the global environment. Safe from here on: the
## only chunk that clears globalenv is Part 2's `setup`, which has already run.
DROP_COV <- getOption("nojobsat.cfg")$DROP_COV

stopifnot(DROP_COV %in% cov_keys)

cov_keys_full <- cov_keys                       # keep the 8-covariate vector
cov_keys      <- setdiff(cov_keys_full, DROP_COV)   # 7 covariates from here on

cat("Adjustment set reduced from", length(cov_keys_full), "to", length(cov_keys),
    "covariates.\n")
cat("Retained:", paste(cov_keys, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

# 2b. Manuscript class numbering

`glca` returns the classes in an arbitrary order, so the raw index printed by the
inherited code (`C2 vs C1`) has no substantive meaning and had to be renumbered by
hand for the manuscript. That manual step is where a table can end up contradicting
Table 2. `canonical_class_numbering.R` derives the manuscript numbering from the
behavioral signature of each class (C1 moderately constructive, C2 disengaged,
C3 constructive and the reference, C4 ambivalent/intermittently destructive) and
stops if the reference used by the three-step models is not the constructive class.
Every table below prints that numbering, so its rows can be pasted as they are.

```{r}
#| label: canonical-numbering
#| results: "hold"

source("canonical_class_numbering.R")

stopifnot(exists("ms_num"), exists("ms_lab"), exists("ms_contrast"),
          ms_num[ref_class] == 3L)
cat(sprintf("Reference: raw C%d -> manuscript C%d (%s).\n",
            ref_class, ms_num[ref_class], ms_lab[ref_class]))
```

# 3. Adjusted fit, 7 covariates {#adjusted-7}

Identical to Part 2's `p2-adj-fit`: same samples, same invariant posteriors, same
`ml3step_multi()` with `lambda = 0` and the ridge fallback at `lambda = 0.1` on
near-separation. The only difference is that `Z` now has 7 columns.

```{r}
#| label: adj-fit-7
#| results: "hold"

gen_df_adj  <- combo[combo$setting == "General salaried", ]
hosp_df_adj <- combo[combo$setting == "Hospital HCW",    ]

## NOTE: no job_sat standardisation here - the covariate is gone. Every other
## covariate is already 0/1 (1 = exposed) from Part 2's harmonisation.

Z_gen  <- as.matrix(gen_df_adj[ , cov_keys])
Z_hosp <- as.matrix(hosp_df_adj[, cov_keys])

fit_adj <- function(Z, post, modal, ref, label) {
  m <- ml3step_multi(Z, post, modal, ref = ref, lambda = 0)
  need_ridge <- m$conv != 0 || anyNA(m$ors$se) || any(abs(m$ors$b) > 5, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (need_ridge) {
    message(label, ": near-separation detected (lambda=0) - refitting with lambda=0.1")
    m <- ml3step_multi(Z, post, modal, ref = ref, lambda = 0.1)
  }
  message(sprintf("%s: n_complete=%d/%d, lambda=%.1f, conv=%d",
                  label, m$n_complete, m$n_total, m$lambda, m$conv))
  m
}

adj_gen7  <- fit_adj(Z_gen,  post_g, modal_g, ref = ref_class, label = "General (7 cov)")
adj_hosp7 <- fit_adj(Z_hosp, post_h, modal_h, ref = ref_class, label = "Hospital (7 cov)")
```

# 4. Table 4 without job satisfaction {#table4-nojobsat}

```{r}
#| label: adj-table-7
#| results: "hold"

cov_labs_adj <- c(
  eri           = "Effort-reward imbalance",
  auditc_hazard = "Hazardous alcohol use (AUDIT-C)",
  no_union      = "Absence of union",
  naq_frequent  = "Frequent negative acts (NAQ)",
  bully_self    = "Self-labeled bullying",
  sex_harass    = "Sexual harassment",
  sex_woman     = "Female sex"
)

fmt_ci_adj <- function(or, lo, hi) sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", or, lo, hi)
z196 <- 1.96

gen_adj_side  <- adj_gen7$ors  |> dplyr::select(covariate, class,
  OR_gen = OR, lo_gen = lo, hi_gen = hi, b_gen = b, se_gen = se)
hosp_adj_side <- adj_hosp7$ors |> dplyr::select(covariate, class,
  OR_hosp = OR, lo_hosp = lo, hi_hosp = hi, b_hosp = b, se_hosp = se)

adj_ror7 <- dplyr::inner_join(gen_adj_side, hosp_adj_side,
                              by = c("covariate", "class")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    logROR   = b_hosp - b_gen,
    seLogROR = sqrt(se_gen^2 + se_hosp^2),
    ROR      = exp(logROR),
    ROR_lo   = exp(logROR - z196 * seLogROR),
    ROR_hi   = exp(logROR + z196 * seLogROR),
    Q        = (logROR / seLogROR)^2,
    p_Q      = stats::pchisq(Q, df = 1, lower.tail = FALSE),
    I2       = pmax(0, (Q - 1) / Q) * 100,
    Covariate = unname(cov_labs_adj[covariate]),
    Profile   = ms_contrast(class, ref_class)   # manuscript numbering, not the raw index
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(covariate, cov_keys), ms_num[class]) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    p_holm = p.adjust(p_Q, method = "holm"),
    q_BH   = p.adjust(p_Q, method = "BH"),
    flag   = dplyr::case_when(
      !is.na(q_BH) & q_BH < 0.05 ~ "*+",
      !is.na(p_Q)  & p_Q  < 0.05 ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ ""))

fmt_p_adj <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "-", ifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p)))

adj_em_tbl7 <- adj_ror7 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Covariate,
    Contrast               = Profile,
    `OR general (95% CI)`  = fmt_ci_adj(OR_gen,  lo_gen,  hi_gen),
    `OR hospital (95% CI)` = fmt_ci_adj(OR_hosp, lo_hosp, hi_hosp),
    `ROR (95% CI)`         = paste0(fmt_ci_adj(ROR, ROR_lo, ROR_hi), flag),
    `Cochran Q`            = sprintf("%.2f", Q),
    `p`                    = fmt_p_adj(p_Q),
    `p (Holm)`             = fmt_p_adj(p_holm),
    `q (BH)`               = fmt_p_adj(q_BH),
    `I2 (%)`               = sprintf("%.0f", I2)
  )

knitr::kable(
  adj_em_tbl7, format = "html",
  caption = sprintf(
    "Table 4 (sensitivity). Effect modification by sample - adjusted ML three-step ORs (95%% CI) mutually adjusting for %d covariates, EXCLUDING job satisfaction. ROR = OR(hospital)/OR(general). Reference = C%d %s. General: lambda=%.1f, n=%d/%d. Hospital: lambda=%.1f, n=%d/%d.",
    length(cov_keys), ms_num[ref_class], ms_lab[ref_class],
    adj_gen7$lambda,  adj_gen7$n_complete,  adj_gen7$n_total,
    adj_hosp7$lambda, adj_hosp7$n_complete, adj_hosp7$n_total))
```

# 5. Side-by-side: with vs without job satisfaction {#comparison}

The 8-covariate estimates are re-fitted here from the same objects, so the
comparison is internal to this render and cannot pick up a stale Table 4.

```{r}
#| label: compare-8-vs-7
#| results: "hold"

Z_gen8  <- as.matrix(gen_df_adj[ , cov_keys_full])
Z_hosp8 <- as.matrix(hosp_df_adj[, cov_keys_full])

## Part 2 standardises job satisfaction within each sample before the fit.
Z_gen8[,  DROP_COV] <- as.numeric(scale(Z_gen8[,  DROP_COV]))
Z_hosp8[, DROP_COV] <- as.numeric(scale(Z_hosp8[, DROP_COV]))

adj_gen8  <- fit_adj(Z_gen8,  post_g, modal_g, ref = ref_class, label = "General (8 cov)")
adj_hosp8 <- fit_adj(Z_hosp8, post_h, modal_h, ref = ref_class, label = "Hospital (8 cov)")

side <- function(fit, tag) fit$ors |>
  dplyr::transmute(covariate, class,
                   !!paste0("OR_", tag) := OR,
                   !!paste0("lo_", tag) := lo,
                   !!paste0("hi_", tag) := hi)

cmp <- dplyr::inner_join(side(adj_gen8, "8"), side(adj_gen7, "7"),
                         by = c("covariate", "class")) |>
  dplyr::filter(covariate != DROP_COV) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Covariate = unname(cov_labs_adj[covariate]),
    Contrast  = ms_contrast(class, ref_class),   # manuscript numbering
    `General, 8 cov (with job sat.)` = fmt_ci_adj(OR_8, lo_8, hi_8),
    `General, 7 cov (without)`       = fmt_ci_adj(OR_7, lo_7, hi_7),
    `% change in OR`                 = sprintf("%+.1f", 100 * (OR_7 / OR_8 - 1))) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(covariate, cov_keys), ms_num[class]) |>
  dplyr::select(Covariate, Contrast, `General, 8 cov (with job sat.)`,
                `General, 7 cov (without)`, `% change in OR`)

knitr::kable(cmp, format = "html",
  caption = "General sample only: adjusted ORs with and without job satisfaction in the adjustment set. A large positive change means job satisfaction was absorbing much of that covariate's association with class membership.")
```

# 7. Reading guide

- The formatted table in Section 4 is a drop-in replacement for Table 4 if the
  7-covariate specification becomes the reported one. Column names already match
  the manuscript header (`Covariate`, `Contrast`, `OR general (95% CI)`,
  `OR hospital (95% CI)`, `ROR (95% CI)`, `Cochran Q`, `p`, `I2 (%)`); the extra
  `p (Holm)` and `q (BH)` columns are dropped in the manuscript version.
- Section 5 is the substantive output: it isolates how much each association in
  Table 4 was being absorbed by job satisfaction.
- Complete-case `n` will differ slightly from Table 4, because rows missing job
  satisfaction are no longer dropped. The printed `n_complete/n_total` in the
  caption is the authoritative denominator for this specification.
- Class numbering is the MANUSCRIPT one (C1 moderately constructive, C2 disengaged,
  C3 constructive and the reference, C4 ambivalent/intermittently destructive),
  assigned from the behavioral signature by `canonical_class_numbering.R` and
  printed directly by every table above. No hand relabelling is needed any more,
  and the raw `glca` index is never shown. The crosswalk for the current fit is
  printed by the `canonical-numbering` chunk; check it against Table 2 once.
